question: Where must YIELD signs be used at a roundabout, and may they control the circulatory roadway?
model_answer: Direct Answer: A YIELD sign is mandatory at the entrance to a roundabout to require road users to yield to other traffic, and YIELD signs must be placed to control the approach roadways only. They shall not be used to control the circulatory roadway itself. Standards (mandatory): - "A YIELD sign shall be used to require road users to yield the right-of-way to other traffic at the entrance to a roundabout. YIELD signs at roundabouts shall be used to control the approach roadways and shall not be used to control the circulatory roadway." Guidance (recommended): - On an approach to a circular intersection controlled by a YIELD sign, and at uncontrolled exits, crosswalks should be located a minimum of 20 feet from the edge of the circulatory roadway. Options (permitted): - YIELD (word) and YIELD AHEAD (symbol or word) pavement markings may be used on approaches to roundabouts. - At roundabouts where ONE WAY signs have been installed in the central island, Roundabout Circulation (R6-5P) plaques may be placed below the YIELD signs on approaches to supplement the central island signs. - The Vehicular Traffic Warning sign assembly may be installed on an approach to a circular intersection controlled by a YIELD sign where the crosswalk is at least 20 feet in advance of the yield point at the entrance to the circulatory roadway. - The Non-Vehicular Warning sign assembly may likewise be installed on such a YIELD-controlled approach where the crosswalk is at least 20 feet in advance of the yield point. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 3D-1 shows YIELD word markings, yield lines, and dotted edge-line extensions on the entering approach roadways only — with the "20 ft MIN." crosswalk setback dimensioned — and no yield control on the circulatory roadway. - [Image 2] Figure 3D-4 shows a two-lane roundabout where yield markings and dotted entrance lines appear only at the approach entries, while the circulatory roadway carries lane-use arrows and lane lines rather than any yield control. - [Image 3] This full-page view contains Sections 3D.04–3D.05, confirming that yield lines and YIELD/YIELD AHEAD word markings are optional treatments on roundabout approaches. - [Image 4] This full-page view contains Section 2B.51, showing the option to place Roundabout Circulation plaques below YIELD signs on roundabout approaches. - [Image 5] This full-page view contains Section 2B.10, including the Standard that YIELD signs at roundabouts shall control the approach roadways and shall not control the circulatory roadway. - [Image 6] This full-page view contains Section 3C.09, including the guidance that crosswalks on YIELD-controlled approaches be a minimum of 20 feet from the edge of the circulatory roadway. Citations: - Section 2B.10 Standard §5 (p.78) - Section 3C.09 Guidance §3 (p.593) - Section 3D.05 Option §1 (p.605) - Section 2B.51 Option §4 (p.118) - Section 2C.54 Option §11 (p.192) - Section 2C.55 Option §6 (p.193) - Figure 3D-1 (p.596) - Figure 3D-4 (p.600) - Page 646 - Page 159 - Page 119 - Page 634
gold_answer: A YIELD sign must control each entering approach roadway. It must not be used to control the circulatory roadway.
